Why CruiseMesh exists

A $7-a-day surprise sparked a better idea.

On a cruise with my family and friends, I found out that sending them a quick message meant buying the cruise line's $7-per-phone, per-day messaging plan — and that isn't even internet access. For four people on a seven-day cruise, that's $196 just to coordinate dinner, share a meeting point, or say "I'm back on board."

That felt absurd. Phones can already talk to each other without the internet: over the ship's Wi-Fi when it allows it, over Bluetooth when they're nearby, and by carrying sealed messages along until paths cross.

CruiseMesh grew from one question: what if family messaging just used the connections already in your pocket?

— David, who builds CruiseMesh

How messages get through

Messages are sealed on your phone and delivered by whichever route exists. Minutes of delay are expected and fine.

  1. Ship Wi-FiPhones on the same ship network find each other and deliver instantly, across the whole ship — no internet package needed. Some ships block phone-to-phone traffic; the app checks and tells you.
  2. Direct contactPhones within Bluetooth range exchange messages immediately.
  3. Carried alongA family member's phone carries your sealed message until paths cross with the recipient.
  4. Internet deliveryWhen any one family phone gets online, it carries the whole family's sealed messages up and back — including to family at home. Needs a Cruise Pass or your own server.

Internet delivery

It's how one internet purchase covers everyone: when any single family phone gets online — one Wi-Fi package, a port-day café — it carries the whole family's messages up and back, including to family at home who aren't on the cruise at all.

Everything travels as sealed envelopes only — the service can't read message contents, sender identities, or receipts — and they're deleted after delivery or 30 days.

Free on the ship. One small pass for the internet part.

Private by design

  1. End-to-end encryptedMessages leave your phone as sealed envelopes. Servers and other phones never see plaintext.
  2. No accountsIdentity is a keypair generated on your phone. No email, phone number, or password.
  3. No trackingNo analytics, advertising, or crash-reporting SDKs — in the apps or on this site.

Details in the privacy policy.

Status

CruiseMesh is open source and in active development. The Android and iOS apps are in release testing; store listings aren't public yet, so build from source if you want it today.
